name: Owenism
summary: Owenism is the early British utopian socialism of Robert Owen and his followers. It holds that character is formed for people by their circumstances and education, blames private property, irrational religion and competition for social evil, and seeks to replace them with cooperative, communally owned villages, cooperative stores, labour exchanges and trade unions, reached by example and persuasion rather than revolution.
scope: Robert Owen's own doctrine and the Owenite movement of c.1813-1850 in Britain and the US (A New View of Society, the 1826 Declaration of Mental Independence, New Lanark, New Harmony, the labour exchange and the Grand National Consolidated Trades Union). It excludes later cooperative movements that dropped Owen's communitarian and anti-religious aims. Owen published little on modern issues, so most answers on them are low-confidence inferences from his principles.

sources.title: Robert Owen
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Character not made by the individual, rejection of religions, no corporal punishment, communities, unions, education, force opposed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Owenites rejected laissez-faire and competition, replacing exchange for profit with labour exchanges and cooperative stores.

unions-good.rationale: Owenites counted the trade union among their three core institutions and Owen led the Grand National Consolidated Trades Union in 1834.

property-fundamental.rationale: Owen named private or individual property as the first of three great evils and called for its destruction.

cut-welfare.rationale: Owenism rejected the Malthusian Poor Law reform and offered cooperative villages as pauper relief, so it opposed cutting relief.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cooperative communities and cooperative production with common ownership by those who work in them were the Owenite programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented view; Owen's preventive, kindness-based approach to order and his stress on liberty of mind point mildly against surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Owenism never addressed drugs, and adherents' views on temperance and liberty would split.

strong-leader.rationale: Owen was paternalist himself, yet he planned self-governing communities and expected change through gradual plans, so leader-led bypassing of politics is not an Owenite aim.

state-harmful.rationale: Owenism sought cooperative communities but not abolition of government; Owen consulted governments and wanted a 'Plan of Government' on preventive principles.

rehabilitation.rationale: Owen held that character is made for, not by, the individual and opposed corporal punishment at New Lanark, so crime calls for reform, not retribution.

traditional-family.rationale: Owen attacked marriage founded on property and fostered communal child-rearing and infant schools, though private family apartments were kept in his communities.

more-religion-public.rationale: Owen declared in 1817 that all religions were false and named irrational religion an evil, so a larger public role for religion runs against his creed.

gradual-change.rationale: Owen expected change through example, education and well-ordered plans rather than upheaval, yet he called for a complete new social system and attacked established religion and property.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Owen proposed federations of communities and addressed governments worldwide, but never advocated an international authority as such.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Owen saw new productive power as capable of abolishing want if used under a rational social system; the problem was its social direction.

revolution-justified.rationale: Owen looked to plans, example and persuasion, held that force oppresses, and Marx and Engels faulted the utopians for avoiding revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Owen thought a rational plan could be devised by enlightened people, yet he also wanted education of all; Owenites split between guidance and democracy.

central-planning.rationale: Owenites preferred planned cooperative communities, not a state-wide planned economy; they favoured planning at community scale and exchange by labour.

socialized-markets.rationale: Owenites accepted exchange through cooperative stores and labour exchanges owned by members, which partially matches, but they sought to supersede markets.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Owen favoured some government involvement in the economy, but through funding cooperative villages rather than directing strategic industry.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Owenite goal was common ownership in cooperative communities, not wide distribution of private property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Owenites replaced money by hour-denominated labour notes at the Equitable Labour Exchange, and Owen's communities were meant to dispense with market wages.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not an Owenite form; Owenites favoured voluntary unions and cooperatives over state-recognised wage bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: Owenism had no party-state theory; Owenites joined the radical democratic movement and the Chartist current.

democracy-best.rationale: Owen was at first apolitical and opposed some franchise radicals, though later Owenites joined the democratic movement that led to Chartism.

workers-councils.rationale: Owenites relied on cooperative societies and unions rather than councils as a basis of power; Owen avoided politics at first.

natural-rulers.rationale: Owen held that character comes from circumstances, not innate nature, so no group is born fit to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Owen held that force oppresses and that kindness corrects bad habits, so he opposed violence as a means.

war-builds-character.rationale: Owen's aim of a peaceful rational society and his rejection of force reject any virtue in war.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Owen condemned irrational religion as one of three evils and thought all religions false, so scriptural law is rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Owen sought cooperation with employers and rulers, and Marx and Engels criticised the utopians for rejecting class struggle.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Owen blamed the competitive, individualist system for evil and built communities on cooperation and common interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Cooperative communities stress mutual obligation, but Owen also stressed liberty of mind; adherents are not recorded on this ranking.

limit-population.rationale: Owenites rejected Malthus's Poor Law remedies and held that the world could feed more; birth control views split among later Owenites.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Owen thought industry's productive power, rightly organised, would bring abundance, so the problem is social order, not industry itself.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Owen welcomed productive power but wanted it governed by social plans; he did not favour disruption for its own sake.

restore-past-order.rationale: Owen looked forward to a New Moral World and called existing religion, marriage and property irrational, not worth restoring.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Owen proclaimed principles as demonstrable fact and tested them through experiments, which supports and opposes this item.

direct-action.rationale: Owenites used cooperative building, unions and later electoral politics; Owen's own method was persuasion and example.

means-match-ends.rationale: Owenites built the new society in miniature through cooperative stores and model communities, a prefigurative method.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Owen looked to machinery and science to deliver abundance and planned communities with advanced education.

production-for-use.rationale: Owenism replaced production for profit with exchange by labour and communities producing for their members' wants.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Owenism rested on the Ricardian labour theory of value and held that workers were deprived of the value of their labour by profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Owenism aimed at harmony among classes through peaceful community building and had no theory of class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Owenite villages farmed in common, as at Ralahine and New Harmony, though they were mixed agricultural-industrial communities.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Owen blamed competition and ignorance for conflict, but did not develop a theory of imperialism.

harm-principle.rationale: Owen defended freedom of thought and opinion while stating that conduct arises from circumstance; no liberty doctrine is documented.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Owen's central claim is that character is formed by circumstance and training, which rejects innate group differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Owen favoured cooperative community federations and unions, but not family-based corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: Owen's plan was voluntary communities, not total state direction of life, though he wanted the state to run education.

bound-labor.rationale: Owen's reforms aimed to improve workers' lives and his communities were voluntary associations, opposing bondage to a lord.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Owen treated his principles as demonstrable fact discoverable by reason, against relativism about knowledge.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Owenite cooperatives and communities were run by members, making democratic control of enterprises central.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Owen's 1817 memorial urged public funds for work for the unemployed, which is compatible with spending to relieve distress.

rule-by-example.rationale: Owen held that character is shaped by surroundings and relied on model communities and kindness rather than laws and punishments.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Owen called his the Rational System, said religions were false, and based his claims on demonstrable fact.

class-collaboration.rationale: Owen appealed to employers and rulers to reform and was criticised by Marx and Engels for seeking cooperation with capitalists.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Owenites founded libraries and the Mechanics' Institutes, so destroying inherited institutions runs against their culture.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Owen's view that circumstance forms character rules out racial hierarchy and it treats all as equally shaped by circumstance.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Owen believed rulers erred from ignorance rather than class interest, so he did not hold this view.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim foreign to Owen's view that ignorance and circumstance explain misery.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Owen blamed rulers' ignorance rather than corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts Owen's emphasis on circumstance over innate nature and his benevolence.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Owen wanted government to fund and plan cooperative communities and national education, far beyond a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Owen held that no individual is to be blamed for a character formed for him, so all deserve kind and equal treatment.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Owen planned model communities that would spread by example in any country; the Marxist doctrine is not his.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Owen thought all religions false, so he would not have schools teach them, though New Lanark's own education was not described this way in sources read.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Owen said force oppresses and kindness corrects, though he did not hold property rules as inviolable.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Owenism rejected competition in favour of cooperation as the principle of social order.

vanguard-party.rationale: Owenites built cooperatives and unions of workers themselves; Marx and Engels faulted the utopians for not organising a revolutionary party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Owen's Lanark report and cooperative villages were designed as relief for the poor and labouring classes.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Owen supported trade unions and led the Grand National Consolidated Trades Union.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Owenites rejected Malthusian explanations and blamed social institutions and ignorance for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Contradicts Owen's belief that circumstances and education make people.

clerical-rule.rationale: Owen named irrational religion as one of three evils.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Owen was pacific but not revolutionary; no stance documented.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Owenites favoured common holding, not individual home ownership for each family.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Owen's villages combined agriculture and industry in rural settings, but he valued New Lanark's industrial community too.

death-penalty.rationale: Owen held that people are not to be blamed for a character formed for them and opposed punitive methods, so execution is rejected.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Owen held all religions to be false and based education on reason and demonstrable fact.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Owen's oration demanded freedom from inherited prejudice and fixed custom of mind; he did not hold Mill's argument.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Owen presented political independence of 1776 as only a first step toward mental freedom, and economic change through common property as a further one.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Contrary to Owen's emphasis on liberty of mind.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Owen held that private property is an evil; the common interest should rule, and common property was the Owenite aim.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Owen opposed religions but wanted to educate people out of them, not to subordinate churches by law; split.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Owen called all religions false and rulers' errors due to ignorance.

character-from-environment.rationale: Owen's central doctrine is that character is formed for, not by, the individual by circumstances, and that proper early training can form any character.

leader-cult.rationale: Owen himself was a revered founder, but he did not preach a cult of the leader as national embodiment.

land-redistribution.rationale: Owenites sought communal land holding, not giving estates to individual farmers; split between common and individual holding.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Owen openly attacked religion and demanded mental liberty.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Owen's circumstances-form-character thesis stresses surroundings, but it is not Marx's mode-of-production theory.

ban-cartels.rationale: Owenites opposed competition rather than seeking to preserve it.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Owen's villages were self-sufficient communities, but he did not advocate colonial trade blocs.

moral-incentives.rationale: Owen's communities relied on education in cooperative character, but also used labour notes; partial support.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Owen held that force oppresses and sought change through example and persuasion, so armed vanguards are foreign to him.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Owenite labour exchange issued its own notes against labour value, though not a state body.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Owen held that the existing system is irrational and must be replaced.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Contradicts Owen's equal treatment of all and rejection of property as a basis of rights.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Owen's stress was on structural change, not charity of the privileged, though he appealed to employers.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Owen was at first apolitical and sought withdrawal into communities; later Owenites entered politics.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Owenism opposed individual property accumulation and relied on cooperative provision for all.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Owen opposed production for profit, which drives status consumption, but the sources read do not state this.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Owen's pacific outlook and his belief that force oppresses rule out arming insurgents abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Owen's pacific outlook rules out troops sent against an allied country's government.

job-guarantee.rationale: Owen's 1817 memorial and Lanark report urged finding useful work for the unemployed, including through villages of cooperation.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Owen's view that conduct reflects circumstances does not settle a duty of obedience.

non-intervention.rationale: Owen's pacifism leans toward it, but his missionary approach to governments cuts the other way.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims contradict Owen's view that ignorance and circumstance explain social ills.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Owen attacked marriage founded on property and mercenary motive and wanted it based on affection.

local-production.rationale: Owen's self-sufficient communities produced mainly for their own consumption.

informal-organisation.rationale: Owenites built formal societies, stores, exchanges and unions.

religious-nation.rationale: Owen rejected religion as a social basis.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Owen's communities held production in common while families kept private apartments.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Owenites favoured cooperative or common provision, not private providers.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Owen's Lanark report and New Harmony proposed communities of roughly 500 to 3,000 people with common property as the remedy for poverty.

religion-illusion.rationale: Owen held that irrational religion was an evil born of false ideas about character and would give way to rational education; he did not describe it as consolation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Owen blamed private property and competition for social evil, though he valued industrial production and machinery as means to abundance.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1826 Declaration treats property-based marriage as one of three evils, tying women's position to the property system.

socialized-care.rationale: Owen founded the New Lanark infant school and proposed state guardianship schools taking children from homes at age two.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Owenites rejected capitalism and sought common property, which Marx classed as utopian socialism; they would not endorse rejecting both.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Owen demanded freedom of speech on religion and attacked irrational religion as an evil, so punishing blasphemy or false worship contradicts his stance.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Owenite communities were designed as self-governing cooperative villages and the movement built unions and cooperatives run by their members, though Owen himself was paternalistic.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He denounced irrational religion as one of the three great evils and traced authority to reason and circumstance, not to God.

social-market-economy.rationale: Owenism rejected competition and the market in favour of cooperative communities and labour exchange, so a regulated market economy is not his model, though it is closer than laissez-faire.

rich-first.rationale: Owen blamed competition and private property for social evil and sought common ownership so all would rise together, the opposite of letting some get rich first.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Owen wrote before international lenders imposed conditions; his stress on self-supporting communities points to autonomy but adherents have no recorded position.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Owenites urged equality for women in their communities, but nature-domination is a later ecological idea absent from the doctrine; no link is documented.

reification.rationale: Owenites blamed competition and profit for misery but did not use the later Marxist idea of social relations appearing as relations between things.

racial-franchise.rationale: Owen's doctrine held that character is formed by circumstances and treated all people as equally formable, which leaves no ground for a racial limit on government.

open-government-data.rationale: Owen said nothing on public records; openness suits his rational, reasoned government but is only a weak inference.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Owen opposed all existing religions and attacked property-based marriage as one of three evils, so state limits on marriage across faiths conflict with his views.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Owen rejected religious division and held that no group is to blame for its character, and his cooperative stores served all members; shunning a religious minority's shops contradicts this.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Owenite communities governed themselves by member meetings, but choice by lot was not part of the movement and no position on it is documented.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Owen held that crime comes from circumstances and should be reformed rather than punished, so punitive prisons are rejected; but he did not call for abolishing all safeguards, an inference.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Owen's Declaration of Mental Independence attacked marriage as then constituted and he advocated equality of the sexes, an inference for authority within marriage.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Owenites held that labour is the source of value and tried to realise it through labour exchanges and hour-denominated labour notes.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Owen's Declaration of Mental Independence attacked irrational religion as a cause of social evil, and he sought reform by reason and example.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Owen's villages and cooperative communities provided common services for all members, implying communal provision of essentials.

municipal-property.rationale: Owen's communities held the means of production in common at the village level, as at New Harmony and the planned villages of co-operation in the sources.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Owen envisaged federations of cooperative villages with a federal coordinating body, an arrangement close to the statement.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Owen did not address payments; the Owenite labour exchange issued its own notes outside state money, but that is a weak guide.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Owen's Declaration of Mental Independence attacked religion as one of three great evils and held that character is formed by circumstances, so a spiritual nature is rejected as stated.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Owenism blamed ignorance and bad institutions, not foreign plots, and saw nations as potential cooperators; no such claim is documented.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Owen never addressed pollution or resource pricing; his communal-ownership principles and his distrust of market mechanisms pull in different directions.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Owenism sought change by example and persuasion rather than revolution, so smashing the state is rejected.

sacred-nation.rationale: Owen's Declaration of Mental Independence attacked irrational religion and he was cosmopolitan; a sacred nation would conflict with that, though he did not address it.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Owen held that character is formed for people by circumstances and education and should be shaped, which conflicts with a fixed nature not to be redesigned.

public-service-media.rationale: Owenites ran their own press but no stance on state-funded public media is documented.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Owen's Declaration of Mental Independence attacked organised religion as one of the three great evils, treating religious doctrines as errors rather than expressions of one truth.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Owen held that character is formed by circumstances, so punishment is unjust and should give way to education and reform; fixed harsh sentences contradict this.

voter-id.rationale: Owen sought change by example and education rather than electoral rules, so the doctrine gives no basis for a position.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Owen blamed private property for social evil and sought communally owned villages, so a first-claim right to private ownership is rejected.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Owen's Declaration of Mental Independence attacked irrational religion as a cause of social evil, which rules out literal scriptural authority.

national-church-status.rationale: Owen opposed established religion as irrational and a source of social evil, so a privileged legal status for a national church is rejected.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Owen held that character is formed by circumstances and blamed private property for inequality, so he judged distribution by how it is arranged, not by how it arose.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Owen welcomed machinery as a source of wealth and wanted its gains shared and hours shortened, though he feared unemployment under competition.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Owen held labour the source of value and proposed labour exchanges with notes measured in hours of labour.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Owenism rejected the Malthusian Poor Law reform and offered cooperative villages as pauper relief, so it opposed cutting relief. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: No person should be blamed or punished as if they had made their own character, since it is formed for them by circumstances.
missingStatements.rationale: Owen drew the conclusion that character is made not by but for the individual and that blame is therefore misplaced; the bank asks about environment and punishment but not this moral conclusion.

missingStatements.text: Goods should be exchanged at a value measured by the hours of labour put into them, using labour notes in place of money.
missingStatements.rationale: The Owenite National Equitable Labour Exchange issued hour-denominated labour notes; no statement captures labour-time money.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow exchange mechanism; its underlying aims are covered by abolish-money-wages, production-for-use and public-money-creation.

missingStatements.text: Society should be reorganised into self-governing cooperative villages that hold their property in common.
missingStatements.rationale: Owen's Lanark report and New Harmony proposed communities of roughly 500 to 3,000 people with common property as the remedy for poverty.

missingStatements.text: Children should be educated from infancy in free schools aimed at forming their character.
missingStatements.rationale: Owen founded the New Lanark infant school and Institute for the Formation of Character, and proposed state guardianship schools.
missingStatements.declined: Near-universal today and a policy detail; the character-formation premise is covered by character-from-environment.

notes: Owen's own views and later Owenite politics differed: Owen was apolitical and wary of franchise radicals, while later Owenites joined the democratic reform movement that led to Chartism. Owen's account of marriage and sex is thinly sourced here (only the 1826 oration), so family and sexuality answers are low confidence.
